items.summary: Unofficial Gujarati (gu-Gujr-IN) machine-assisted translation of the Open Logic Project, frozen at revision 9620cc73f9c8e0ad003c514a5d3748f29611c4c0. This cumulative release covers 163 of the 722 tracked content units, OLP-0004–OLP-0166. It contains complete Sets, Relations, Functions, Size of Sets, Arithmetization, Infinite Sets, Propositional Logic syntax and semantics, the first-order proof-systems overview, Sequent Calculus, Natural Deduction, signed analytic Tableaux, Axiomatic Deduction, First-Order Completeness, the First-Order Logic introduction, Syntax, and Semantics. The new semantics chapter develops structures and universes, term values, covered structures, variable assignments, recursive satisfaction, assignment independence, extensionality, validity, consequence, satisfiability, models, and theories. The full Gujarati edition remains in progress. The deposit preserves the exact anonymously verified GitHub release first-order-semantics-v0.10.0 at commit 8e05f9182abbda985f31222a7e2e00a08fec25b9: a 211-page A4 PDF, the cumulative TeX driver, a complete editable source ZIP, a genuine reflowable EPUB 3.3 publication, the offline HTML/MathML reader, SHA-256 checksums, and a machine-readable QA record. The PDF is uploaded first as the human-readable Zenodo preview. The archive contains all 722 pristine English source units as source provenance; only the stated 163 units are translated. Translation and review were performed by a Codex agent. Checks include 1,815 exact aligned linguistic-block reviews, 9,587 source mathematical spans, 829 reverse-paraphrase samples, 117 disclosed frozen-source corrections, three byte-identical PDF passes, visual inspection of all 211 PDF pages, and an offline reader with 9,340 MathML nodes, five truth tables, six line-numbered axiomatic derivation tables, thirteen described diagrams, 208 structural proof representations, 654 unique anchors, and no broken internal links. The EPUB preserves all 9,340 native MathML expressions, 171 navigation links, Gujarati metadata and fonts, described diagrams, and correction disclosures; a byte-identical cold replay, EPUBCheck 5.3.0 with zero messages, and silent Chromium inspection passed. These are same-agent checks, not independent native-speaker or human certification. Some specialized Gujarati terms remain provisional. Eighteen Gujarati scholarly and educational sources and seventy-seven exact passages were directly inspected, with terminology, hash and segment-use indexes included. Copyrighted canon originals and full extracts are excluded. The inherited Open Logic Project attribution and CC BY 4.0 license are preserved; bundled Noto Sans Gujarati font files retain their SIL Open Font License. This translation does not imply endorsement by the source authors or canon publishers.

items.summary: Medicine-level dataset and complete R analysis code for the retrospective cohort study Authorised in Europe, Awaited in Bulgaria: A Time-to-Event Analysis of Where the 3.9-Year Delay to Oncology Medicine Reimbursement Accrues (Department of Social Medicine and Public Health, Medical University of Plovdiv, Bulgaria). The dataset links 294 centrally authorised oncology medicinal products from the European Medicines Agency's public medicine data (marketing authorisation date and status, ATC code, therapeutic area, marketing authorisation holder, and the new active substance, generic, biosimilar, orphan, conditional approval, accelerated assessment, PRIME and advanced therapy designations) to the Bulgarian reimbursement record of the National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products: the start and end dates and outcome of the published HTA procedure, and the first appearance of each product in 130 dated monthly snapshots of Annex 2 of the Positive Drug List (16 October 2015 to 2 July 2026), with the provenance of each date. The primary cohort of the article is the 189 medicines authorised from 16 October 2015. The unit of observation is the medicinal product; no personal data are involved. The code reproduces every estimate, table and figure of the article and its supplement: Kaplan-Meier cumulative probabilities of reimbursement, decomposition of the interval into company submission and HTA assessment phases, Cox models stratified by product type (with robust, new-active-substance-only and advanced-therapy-excluded sensitivity fits), competing-risk and alternative-endpoint sensitivity analyses. See README.md and codebook.md.
items.title: Time from EMA marketing authorisation to reimbursement in Bulgaria for 294 centrally authorised oncology medicines, 2005-2026: medicine-level dataset and analysis code

items.summary: Reproducibility release 1.1.0 for Ocean Engineering manuscript OE-D-25-10458. This package supports a controlled Rotterdam-Yokohama comparison of the Suez, Cape and Northern Sea Route corridors using three predefined strategic waypoint philosophies per corridor. The archive contains the Python routing and analysis code, all nine waypoint definitions, frozen maritime-network geometries and scenario/leg distances, dual-coastline quality-assurance and local-repair reports, 0.05/0.025-degree convergence outputs, sourced OpenStreetMap Suez Canal geometry and provenance, downstream time/fuel/CO2 analyses, exponent and vessel-reference sensitivities, and the frozen manuscript sources and figures. The routing method uses searoute 1.4.3, WGS84 distance recomputation and no great-circle fallback. The reproduction command stages the archived routes, regenerates downstream tables and copies the included figure assets. A full routing rerun additionally requires the externally distributed Natural Earth 10 m v5.1.1 and GSHHG 2.3.7 full L1 coastline datasets. Tests and release checks are documented in the archive. The comparison is strategic and does not predict realised voyages or commercial viability.
items.title: Effects of Route Representation on Distance and Downstream Voyage Implications in Europe–Asia Trade: A Comparison of the Suez, Cape, and Northern Sea Route Corridors

items.summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
items.title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

items.summary: This repository contains the data, documentation, and replication materials associated with the data paper on the  Cartulario de Santo Toribio de Liébana . The dataset provides a structured reconstruction of the documentary collection edited by Luis Sánchez Belda and converts the information contained in the cartulary into machine-readable research data. It covers 566 documentary acts and includes linked information on 576 payment or counter-performance elements, 603 place names, and 1,348 identified persons , together with a concordance between documentary numbering systems. The package preserves the documentary structure of the source while providing standardized variables suitable for quantitative and computational historical research. Particular attention is given to economic transactions. Payments and other forms of material counter-performance are recorded at the individual-component level rather than collapsed into a single transaction value. The data also distinguish operative contractual provisions from penalty clauses and other formulaic diplomatic material. Contains the materials required to reproduce and audit the construction of the dataset, including the structured datasets, extraction and coding documentation, variable definitions, provenance information, validation materials, and the code used for data processing and quality-control procedures. The replication workflow documents the transformation from the published documentary source to the final structured tables. It records corrections and normalization decisions while maintaining traceability to the underlying documentary act. The package is therefore intended not only to reproduce the published dataset but also to make individual coding decisions auditable. The dataset is designed for reuse in research on medieval economic history, property transactions, monastic institutions, historical geography, social networks, and computational approaches to diplomatic sources.
items.title: Replication package for the Santo Toribio de Liébana medieval cartulary dataset

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: Abstract Modern enterprise AI systems increasingly operate across multiple authorized data sources, memories, applications, and tools. This creates a security problem that is not adequately described as conventional data theft. An AI workload may be individually authorized to read support records, engineering information, source-control activity, supplier data, budgets, hiring information, and calendars. No individual source may contain a sensitive strategic conclusion. However, the AI system may combine those independently authorized fragments and reconstruct a new high-value object: an unreleased product direction, likely launch window, supplier dependency, market strategy, organizational weakness, or other forward-looking enterprise knowledge. The security boundary therefore changes. The relevant questions are no longer only: Who may read data A? or: Who may read data B? They also become: Who may establish the relationship A-to-B? Who may retain or disclose the resulting inference? Who may cause an external action because of that reconstructed meaning? This paper describes a threat model in which the AI assistant becomes a computational graph across previously separate enterprise systems. The resulting risk may exist even when each underlying retrieval complies with its ordinary source-level permissions. The sensitive object is not necessarily a stolen database record; it may be a new semantic object created through authorized association. The architecture therefore separates two security transitions: Authorized Data | v Authorized Reconstruction | v Computed Meaning | v Authorized Effectuation | v External Consequence The first transition concerns association authority : permission to read independently authorized fragments does not automatically imply permission to join those fragments into a new semantic relationship. The second concerns execution-time finality : permission to compute, generate, or prepare an output does not automatically imply permission for that output to become externally consequential. The proposed architectural model therefore introduces controls around independently governed relationship mapping, session-bound reconstruction, minimum-necessary temporary views, provenance-aware release, and a mandatory effectuation boundary. Candidate outputs or actions remain non-effective until the consequence-controlling component verifies the applicable authority, provenance, destination, policy state, disclosure conditions, and other protected execution state immediately before release or effectuation. In compact form: Access != Association Association != Authority to Disclose Computation != Authority to Cause Consequence The execution-time consequence boundary may be implemented through existing mechanisms such as policy-enforcement points, reference monitors, authorization servers, secure execution environments, transaction coordinators, capability systems, protected dispatchers, database commit controls, network command gates, or equivalent mechanisms. The important property is functional rather than terminological: A computed result or proposed action remains non-effective until the component with mandatory control over the actual consequence verifies that the exact pending effect is permitted under current protected authority and state. This architecture is intended to complement conventional identity, access control, encryption, zero-trust, data-loss prevention, confidential-computing, logging, and authorization systems rather than replace them. Those mechanisms continue to protect identities, stores, channels, and individual permissions. The additional problem addressed here is governance of the relationship created between authorized fragments and governance of the transition from computed meaning to actual consequence . The paper presents this as a forward-looking threat model rather than an allegation concerning any specific enterprise or AI product. The objective is to identify an architectural risk
items.title: Enterprise AI as a Reconstruction Layer: Governing Derived Knowledge and Execution-Time Consequences

items.summary: Preconditioned Total Field Inversion: a single-step method that inverts the total field directly to susceptibility over the whole field-of-view, jointly performing background-field removal and dipole inversion. Uses a preconditioner (χ = P·y, larger outside the brain) so the large out-of-brain background susceptibility is well-conditioned, with MEDI-style L1 morphology regularization. QSM-CI reconstruction method tfi-qsmrs . Browse and run it at https://qsmxt.github.io/QSM-CI/submission.html?method=tfi-qsmrs .

items.summary: Code and data supporting the article "Capillary-driven networks obey Murray's law everywhere except at the meniscus". The archive contains three things. A self-contained MATLAB package that builds the figures of the article and recomputes every number quoted in its text, using a backtracking Newton iteration on a scale-invariant objective and requiring no toolboxes. A Python module that carries the same model on arbitrary graphs, including graphs with loops, where the flow is obtained from the nodal Laplacian rather than from the topology, together with a script that runs the verifications of Appendices C, F and H: the nine-channel graph with four independent loops, the envelope identity, the sweep over the driving degree, the three terminal conditions, the power-to-cost ratios and the Kamiya-Togawa law, and the case of several dissipation mechanisms in one channel. And a pixel-level digitisation of Fig. 7 of Zhang and Lorente, Sci. Rep. 13, 11278 (2023), against which Sec. V of the article is compared, with the source raster, the recovered coordinates in three formats, and an image comparing the reconstruction against the original. Neither optimiser uses the sizing law under test: each maximises the throughput at fixed cost from the resistance and the cost directly, so the residuals reported are an independent check of Eq. (7) rather than a restatement of it. The digitiser is deterministic and reproduces its 298 recovered points byte for byte. Code is released under the MIT licence (LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt). The source raster in data/ is reproduced unaltered from a CC BY 4.0 third-party article and remains copyright of its authors; see THIRD-PARTY.txt. README.txt describes the contents, how to run everything, and which printed quantities depend on the configuration block.

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: This dataset provides a curated and reproducible compilation of data used to analyze long-term trends in external-cause mortality in Ecuador from 1990 through 2024. The primary data sources are official mortality statistics and population estimates and projections published by Ecuador’s National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos, INEC). The dataset includes annual mortality counts and population-based indicators for major external-cause categories, including land transport injuries, other transport accidents and accidental injuries, suicide, homicide, events of undetermined intent, and other external causes. Where available, the data are organized by calendar year, sex, age or age group, geographic unit, ICD classification, and cause of death. Population denominators, crude mortality rates, confidence intervals, absolute and relative changes, mortality composition measures, sex-specific rate ratios, and variables used in the statistical analyses are documented separately from the original source data. The repository also contains information used to support the reproducibility of the associated scientific study, including analytical datasets, variable definitions, ICD harmonization information, population denominators, model-related variables, sensitivity-analysis data, quality-control documentation, data provenance, and records of differences identified between historical editions of INEC statistical tables. Hospital discharge datasets reviewed during data curation are documented at the variable and source level. Individual-level hospital discharge microdata are not included in the public dissemination package when their inclusion could create unnecessary privacy or re-identification risks. Original source information is kept distinct from derived variables and researcher-calculated indicators to preserve full provenance and auditability. The package follows FAIR data principles and includes machine-readable CSV files together with the original curated Excel database, a data dictionary, methodology documentation, provenance and transformation records, quality-control information, ethics and privacy considerations, citation metadata, licensing information, and version history. No missing values were imputed solely for publication, and no undocumented assumptions were used to generate unavailable data. Values for recent years should be interpreted according to the provisional or revised status indicated by the original INEC sources. This dataset is intended to support reproducibility, secondary epidemiological analyses, public health surveillance, methodological review, and research on injuries, violence, suicide, homicide, road traffic mortality, and other external causes of death in Ecuador.
items.title: Ecuador External-Cause Mortality, Population Denominators, and Reproducibility Dataset, 1990–2024

items.summary: Reproducibility archive for a fully computational study of a coupled interface-mode multilayer sensing refractive index and temperature over a 100 K range, accompanying the article "Bias-Aware Detection Limits, Calibration Transfer and Matched-Control Robustness Assessment in Dual-Parameter Photonic Refractive-Index and Temperature Sensing: A Coupled Interface-Mode Multilayer Case Study" by Agah Oktay Ertay and Muhammed Mustafa Ertay, accepted by Sensors (MDPI) on 18 September 2026. Version 1.2.1 is the publication release. It carries version 1.2.0, which the Data Availability Statement of the article names, without changing any number, table, input, model, or analysis script (560 of 572 files byte for byte; the 12 replaced root documents are kept under provenance/v1.2.0/). It adds the figure artwork as published: every graphic of the article and of its Supplementary Material as supplied to the journal (figures/published/), the source that draws the 20 graphics redrawn at the proof stage for typographic reasons (true minus signs, notation, legend placement; code/publication_figures/, with a complete diff against the production source), and a launcher mode that re-renders them from the archived tables. It contains the MATLAB production forward model and driver scripts, the frozen material, geometry and acceptance-criterion input files, and the sensitivity matrix, nonlinear calibration, covariance and probability-of-detection routines, the per-realization Monte Carlo yield and matched-control output tables, the design-search evaluation log, the FDFD, CST, MEEP, MPB and FEniCSx verification models with their exported spectra and convergence histories, and the numerical series behind every figure and table in the article and in its Supplementary Material. Version 1.2.0 adds the analyses of the major revision as a separately runnable stage that uses the archived production routines and the frozen tables of version 1.1.0: the sensitivity of the detection limits to instrument noise and drift, reduced per-device calibration protocols, the complete metric set of the nanolaminate-free stack, an oblique-incidence test of the hyperbolicity condition, and the jointly matched trivial control with its paired benchmark. The 483 source, input, result, figure, and solver files of version 1.1.0 are carried byte for byte; only the root metadata files and the launcher were updated, and the v1.1.0 metadata and checksum manifest are kept under provenance/v1.1.0/. A single launcher runs the integrity check, the full reproduction, the revision stage, or both; a SHA-256 manifest covers every other file in the archive. Code is released under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE); data, result tables, and figures under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). The three measured ITO n,k tables are third-party public-domain data (CC0 1.0, via refractiveindex.info, originating from Minenkov et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16, 9517-9531, 2024) and should be cited from that source. The study is numerical. No multilayer was fabricated and no spectrum measured; agreement between independent solvers is not offered as experimental validation.
items.title: Bias-Aware_Detection_Limits_Calibration_Transfer_and_Matched-Control_Robustness_Assessment_in_Dual-Parameter_Photonic_Refractive-Index_and_Temperature_Sensing_A_Coupled_Interface-Mode_Multilayer_Case_Study_All_Software_Package_and_Data_v1.2.1

items.summary: Archived reproducibility bundle for CellFate-Rx Generation 1: a preregistered reanalysis of the six-condition clonal-tracing dataset GEO GSE279162 (generated and deposited by Schaff et al., doi:10.1016/j.xgen.2026.101191). No new data were generated. Tests whether pretreatment transcriptional state carries condition-specific information about future clonal detection, beyond condition identity and captured pretreatment clone abundance, under clone-held-out evaluation, with the ranking test frozen by digest before any ranking statistic was computed. The archive contains the frozen model artifact, the derived clone pseudobulk cache needed to re-run the permutation null, all out-of-fold predictions, the 1,000 per-draw permutation values and 2,000 bootstrap replicates, every stage protocol and record including failed and negative results, the environment lock, and three verification tools that refuse on any modified artifact. A SHA256SUMS manifest accompanies the bundle. Licensing. Software and the frozen model are source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0: free for academic, educational, nonprofit and other noncommercial use with no permission request. Any commercial use, including developing or evaluating a commercial product or service before it has earned any revenue, requires a separate license (see COMMERCIAL-LICENSING.md); where that notice and the licence differ, the licence governs. Manuscript text and figures are CC BY 4.0. Third-party datasets retain their original terms.

items.summary: This software package contains the code used for the simulation, analysis, and reproducibility of a study on closed-loop digital-twin validation of federated learning updates for methane control in underground mining. The package includes the plant–twin simulator, federated-learning routines, calibration scripts, intervention-budget analyses, attack calibration and backdoor diagnostics, candidate-update generation and scoring, the fresh-seed confirmatory analysis, twin-mismatch sensitivity experiments, exploratory Krum-based comparisons, FLTrust-style diagnostics, serious-harm analyses, and read-only manuscript audits. The evaluation separates the simulated plant used for operational outcome assessment from the imperfect digital twin used for candidate scoring. The repository also documents the distinction between direct plant evaluation and curve-interpolated budget matching used in different experimental stages. Raw methane measurements are not redistributed in this archive. The study uses the public dataset “Methane” by Sikora and Wróbel, available from Mendeley Data, Version 1, DOI: 10.17632/yd7vw4c5mk.1. Instructions for obtaining and preparing the data are provided in DATA.md. The archive includes reproducibility documentation, script-to-manuscript mapping, provenance notes, execution order, software requirements, and SHA-256 checksums. Historical scripts are retained where necessary to document the progression from early exploratory analyses to the final frozen analysis.

items.summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study" . This package contains everything needed to regenerate every table, figure and reported number in the manuscript from the analysis outputs, except the raw trajectories. Systems and sampling: three FGFR1 kinase domain systems (wild type, V561M, N546K) in complex with erdafitinib, three independent 500 -ns replicates each , analysed over the 200 -500 ns plateau. Nominal sampling 4.5 us; realised aggregate production sampling 4.491 us. All three systems share a 9.28387 nm cubic SPC water box with 0.15 M NaCl (total atoms 78 , 608 / 78 , 609 / 78 , 624 ). Contents: - scripts/ - 14 analysis and plotting scripts (Python 3.10 ) covering every main and supplementary figure panel - tables/ - 38 per-replicate and summary result tables (CSV) - matrices/ - 24 DCCM matrices, common-subspace PCA projections and RMSD series (NumPy .npy) - mdp/ - GROMACS run-control files (minimisation, ions, NVT, NPT, production) plus the fully expanded grompp parameter file - tpr/ - the nine production run inputs (complete, with all parameters baked in ) - topology/ - GROMACS topology files ( system and protein topologies, posre.itp, ligand parameters, index files ) - README.md - directory layout, frame-selection rules, uncertainty conventions, table/figure provenance, and full run parameters Software: GROMACS 2024.6 (production) and 2024.3 (analysis), gmx_MMPBSA 1.6 .5 , MDTraj 1.10 .3 , Python 3.10 (NumPy 2.2 .6 , SciPy 1.15 .2 , Matplotlib). Frame selection: MM/GBSA and MM/PBSA energies were computed on frames extracted at 1-ns spacing ( 301 frames per intact replicate ; 291 for V561M replicate 2 ). Replicate-level statistics use one value per independent trajectory ( n = 3 per system ) and are reported as mean +/- SD ; frames within a trajectory are not treated as independent samples . Per-residue decomposition values are reported as mean +/- SEM , which can be converted to SD by multiplying by the square root of 3 . Important for regeneration: the production runs were executed as a 200 -ns run followed by a 300 -ns extension (gmx convert -tpr -extend). md.mdp therefore defines only the first 200 ns and must be read together with that extension step. See README.md section 7. Raw trajectories (approximately 13 GB, full atom resolution, 100 -ps output cadence) are available from the corresponding author on request .
items.title: Reproducibility package for: Distinct conformational and interaction signatures of the FGFR1 V561M and N546K resistance-associated mutations: a multi-replicate molecular dynamics study

items.summary: This technical note investigates whether operator-relative noncentrality can predict the relative empirical power of complementary localized scan statistics in correlated spectra. The motivating real-data benchmark compares BABAR and BESIII measurements of the e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ cross section in the ρ-resonance region on a common 5 MeV grid from 0.600 to 0.880 GeV. The real-data comparison remains negative, with no statistically supported localized shape tension identified. The methodological study compares a coherent-yield scan with a covariance-profiled shape scan and defines the frozen coordinate Θ = log(ES/EY), where ES and EY represent maximum local operator-accessible signal strengths. An archival confirmatory replication used 50,000 null calibration draws per covariance environment, 15,000 independent null-validation draws per environment, 1,440 signal/covariance conditions, and 576,000 injected pseudoexperiments. Θ predicted which scan had greater empirical power with pooled AUC 0.9820 and mean leave-one-covariance-environment-out AUC 0.9740; its correlation with the empirical power difference was 0.9185. Independent Type-I error estimates ranged from 0.0466 to 0.0540. The results support operator-relative noncentrality as a useful empirical coordinate for complementary globally calibrated scans within the tested benchmark. The underlying ingredients, including Gaussian noncentrality, covariance-weighted subspace detection, quadratic scanning, and Monte Carlo calibration, are established; the contribution is a reproducible computational synthesis and controlled characterization rather than a claim of a new general statistical law

items.summary: Code, frozen synthetic results, publication-figure generation, and the Oman GT3A external control used to test when resistivity improves elastic rock-physics inversion and how the result changes when transport processes are missing from the fitted models. The sample-level Oman measurements are not redistributed because their repository record does not state a redistribution licence; the archive instead provides provenance, a source hash, and a preparation script.
items.title: When does resistivity resolve elastic ambiguity? Reproducibility archive

items.summary: This software package contains the code used for the simulation, analysis, and reproducibility of a study on closed-loop digital-twin validation of federated learning updates for methane control in underground mining. The package includes the plant–twin simulator, federated-learning routines, calibration scripts, intervention-budget analyses, attack calibration and backdoor diagnostics, candidate-update generation and scoring, the fresh-seed confirmatory analysis, twin-mismatch sensitivity experiments, exploratory Krum-based comparisons, FLTrust-style diagnostics, serious-harm analyses, and read-only manuscript audits. The evaluation separates the simulated plant used for operational outcome assessment from the imperfect digital twin used for candidate scoring. The repository also documents the distinction between direct plant evaluation and curve-interpolated budget matching used in different experimental stages. Raw methane measurements are not redistributed in this archive. The study uses the public dataset “Methane” by Sikora and Wróbel, available from Mendeley Data, Version 1, DOI: 10.17632/yd7vw4c5mk.1. Instructions for obtaining and preparing the data are provided in DATA.md. The archive includes reproducibility documentation, script-to-manuscript mapping, provenance notes, execution order, software requirements, and SHA-256 checksums. Historical scripts are retained where necessary to document the progression from early exploratory analyses to the final frozen analysis.

items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
items.title: When gravity adds useful information to interpretation-conditioned post-stack seismic inversion: reproducibility archive

items.summary: This dataset provides a curated and reproducible compilation of data used to analyze long-term trends in external-cause mortality in Ecuador from 1990 through 2024. The primary data sources are official mortality statistics and population estimates and projections published by Ecuador’s National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos, INEC). The dataset includes annual mortality counts and population-based indicators for major external-cause categories, including land transport injuries, other transport accidents and accidental injuries, suicide, homicide, events of undetermined intent, and other external causes. Where available, the data are organized by calendar year, sex, age or age group, geographic unit, ICD classification, and cause of death. Population denominators, crude mortality rates, confidence intervals, absolute and relative changes, mortality composition measures, sex-specific rate ratios, and variables used in the statistical analyses are documented separately from the original source data. The repository also contains information used to support the reproducibility of the associated scientific study, including analytical datasets, variable definitions, ICD harmonization information, population denominators, model-related variables, sensitivity-analysis data, quality-control documentation, data provenance, and records of differences identified between historical editions of INEC statistical tables. Hospital discharge datasets reviewed during data curation are documented at the variable and source level. Individual-level hospital discharge microdata are not included in the public dissemination package when their inclusion could create unnecessary privacy or re-identification risks. Original source information is kept distinct from derived variables and researcher-calculated indicators to preserve full provenance and auditability. The package follows FAIR data principles and includes machine-readable CSV files together with the original curated Excel database, a data dictionary, methodology documentation, provenance and transformation records, quality-control information, ethics and privacy considerations, citation metadata, licensing information, and version history. No missing values were imputed solely for publication, and no undocumented assumptions were used to generate unavailable data. Values for recent years should be interpreted according to the provisional or revised status indicated by the original INEC sources. This dataset is intended to support reproducibility, secondary epidemiological analyses, public health surveillance, methodological review, and research on injuries, violence, suicide, homicide, road traffic mortality, and other external causes of death in Ecuador.
items.title: Ecuador External-Cause Mortality, Population Denominators, and Reproducibility Dataset, 1990–2024

items.summary: This technical note investigates whether operator-relative noncentrality can predict the relative empirical power of complementary localized scan statistics in correlated spectra. The motivating real-data benchmark compares BABAR and BESIII measurements of the e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ cross section in the ρ-resonance region on a common 5 MeV grid from 0.600 to 0.880 GeV. The real-data comparison remains negative, with no statistically supported localized shape tension identified. The methodological study compares a coherent-yield scan with a covariance-profiled shape scan and defines the frozen coordinate Θ = log(ES/EY), where ES and EY represent maximum local operator-accessible signal strengths. An archival confirmatory replication used 50,000 null calibration draws per covariance environment, 15,000 independent null-validation draws per environment, 1,440 signal/covariance conditions, and 576,000 injected pseudoexperiments. Θ predicted which scan had greater empirical power with pooled AUC 0.9820 and mean leave-one-covariance-environment-out AUC 0.9740; its correlation with the empirical power difference was 0.9185. Independent Type-I error estimates ranged from 0.0466 to 0.0540. The results support operator-relative noncentrality as a useful empirical coordinate for complementary globally calibrated scans within the tested benchmark. The underlying ingredients, including Gaussian noncentrality, covariance-weighted subspace detection, quadratic scanning, and Monte Carlo calibration, are established; the contribution is a reproducible computational synthesis and controlled characterization rather than a claim of a new general statistical law

items.summary: Reproducibility archive for a fully computational study of a coupled interface-mode multilayer sensing refractive index and temperature over a 100 K range, accompanying the article "Bias-Aware Detection Limits, Calibration Transfer and Matched-Control Robustness Assessment in Dual-Parameter Photonic Refractive-Index and Temperature Sensing: A Coupled Interface-Mode Multilayer Case Study" by Agah Oktay Ertay and Muhammed Mustafa Ertay, accepted by Sensors (MDPI) on 18 September 2026. Version 1.2.1 is the publication release. It carries version 1.2.0, which the Data Availability Statement of the article names, without changing any number, table, input, model, or analysis script (560 of 572 files byte for byte; the 12 replaced root documents are kept under provenance/v1.2.0/). It adds the figure artwork as published: every graphic of the article and of its Supplementary Material as supplied to the journal (figures/published/), the source that draws the 20 graphics redrawn at the proof stage for typographic reasons (true minus signs, notation, legend placement; code/publication_figures/, with a complete diff against the production source), and a launcher mode that re-renders them from the archived tables. It contains the MATLAB production forward model and driver scripts, the frozen material, geometry and acceptance-criterion input files, and the sensitivity matrix, nonlinear calibration, covariance and probability-of-detection routines, the per-realization Monte Carlo yield and matched-control output tables, the design-search evaluation log, the FDFD, CST, MEEP, MPB and FEniCSx verification models with their exported spectra and convergence histories, and the numerical series behind every figure and table in the article and in its Supplementary Material. Version 1.2.0 adds the analyses of the major revision as a separately runnable stage that uses the archived production routines and the frozen tables of version 1.1.0: the sensitivity of the detection limits to instrument noise and drift, reduced per-device calibration protocols, the complete metric set of the nanolaminate-free stack, an oblique-incidence test of the hyperbolicity condition, and the jointly matched trivial control with its paired benchmark. The 483 source, input, result, figure, and solver files of version 1.1.0 are carried byte for byte; only the root metadata files and the launcher were updated, and the v1.1.0 metadata and checksum manifest are kept under provenance/v1.1.0/. A single launcher runs the integrity check, the full reproduction, the revision stage, or both; a SHA-256 manifest covers every other file in the archive. Code is released under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE); data, result tables, and figures under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). The three measured ITO n,k tables are third-party public-domain data (CC0 1.0, via refractiveindex.info, originating from Minenkov et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16, 9517-9531, 2024) and should be cited from that source. The study is numerical. No multilayer was fabricated and no spectrum measured; agreement between independent solvers is not offered as experimental validation.
